1.1.1.applicability: All non-text content, including controls, charts, CAPTCHA, decoration, and media previews.
actions: Inventory non-text objects in every observed state and inspect each accessible alternative.
Compare each alternative with the object's purpose; test controls and record CAPTCHA and sensory exceptions.
1.1.1.passed: Alternatives convey equivalent purpose; decorative objects are ignored and all special cases meet the criterion.
1.1.1.failed: An applicable object has a missing, misleading, or insufficient alternative, or exposes decoration as meaningful content.
1.1.1.inapplicable: The scoped states contain no non-text content, supported by an object inventory.

1.2.1.applicability: Prerecorded audio-only or video-only media, excluding clearly labeled alternatives to text.
actions: Inventory and play audio-only and silent-video content through its full duration.
Compare transcripts or equivalent audio alternatives with all meaningful sounds, visual events, and interactions.
1.2.1.passed: Each applicable recording has an equivalent alternative with all required information.
1.2.1.failed: An applicable recording lacks an alternative or omits meaningful information.
1.2.1.inapplicable: No applicable recordings exist; document any labeled text-alternative exception.

1.2.2.applicability: Prerecorded synchronized media with audio, excluding clearly labeled alternatives to text.
actions: Enable captions and play each recording fully, including controls and alternate tracks.
Compare captions with speech, speaker identity, meaningful sounds, and timing.
1.2.2.passed: Captions accurately convey required audio information and remain synchronized.
1.2.2.failed: Captions are unavailable, materially inaccurate, incomplete, or unsynchronized.
1.2.2.inapplicable: There is no applicable prerecorded synchronized media; document any text-alternative exception.

1.2.3.applicability: Prerecorded synchronized media with visual information, excluding labeled alternatives to text.
actions: Play each recording and identify visual information absent from the main audio.
Compare its audio description or complete media alternative against events, dialogue, and available interactions.
1.2.3.passed: Audio description or a complete media alternative supplies all required information and interactions.
1.2.3.failed: Neither accepted alternative conveys the required visual information or interactions.
1.2.3.inapplicable: No applicable synchronized recordings exist; document any text-alternative exception.

actions: Observe a live session with captions enabled and record the observed time range.
Compare captions with speech, speaker changes, meaningful sounds, and timing.
1.2.4.passed: Live captions convey all required audio information during the observed live session.
1.2.4.failed: Required live captions are missing or lose meaningful audio information.
1.2.4.inapplicable: The product has no live synchronized audio media; absence of a scheduled event alone is insufficient.

actions: List meaningful visual information not conveyed by the main audio and play each description track fully.
Compare audio description against that list; a text transcript alone does not satisfy this criterion.
1.2.5.passed: Audio description conveys all necessary visual information, or the main audio already conveys it.
1.2.5.failed: Necessary visual information is absent from the main audio and the audio description.
1.2.5.inapplicable: There is no prerecorded synchronized video in the scope.

actions: Inventory headings, lists, tables, groups, form labels, and visually expressed relationships.
Read the same structures with the real reader and compare relationships with rendered layout or equivalent text.
1.3.1.applicability: Information, structure, or relationships conveyed through presentation.
1.3.1.passed: All presented relationships are programmatically determinable or explicitly available in text.
1.3.1.failed: A meaningful relationship is conveyed only by presentation and has no equivalent text.
1.3.1.inapplicable: No presentation conveys information or relationships; supply observations supporting that conclusion.

actions: Identify sequences whose order affects meaning, including columns and inserted dynamic content.
Read each sequence with the real reader and compare its programmatic order with the intended meaning.
1.3.2.passed: At least one programmatically determinable sequence preserves meaning for every applicable sequence.
1.3.2.failed: An applicable sequence loses meaning in its programmatically determined reading order.
1.3.2.inapplicable: Meaning does not depend on any sequence in the observed states.

1.3.3.applicability: Instructions for understanding or operating content.
actions: Collect instructions, including error, onboarding, and interaction instructions.
Check references to shape, color, size, location, orientation, and sound for an additional identifying cue.
1.3.3.passed: Instructions can be followed without relying solely on sensory characteristics.
1.3.3.failed: A required instruction identifies an action solely by a sensory characteristic.

1.3.4.applicability: Rendered desktop content capable of portrait and landscape layouts.
actions: Render portrait and landscape viewport configurations and operate the same functionality.
Inspect restrictions on orientation and obtain product context for any claimed essential orientation.
1.3.4.passed: Content and operation are available in both orientations, except documented essential restrictions.
1.3.4.failed: A nonessential orientation restriction prevents viewing or operation.
1.3.4.inapplicable: Only an essential orientation applies, with a reason tied to the content rather than a preferred design.

1.3.5.applicability: User-information inputs matching the WCAG Input Purposes list in technologies supporting identification.
actions: Inventory user-information fields and map each purpose to the normative Input Purposes list.
Inspect programmatic purpose metadata and compare it with the requested information; labels alone are insufficient.
1.3.5.passed: Every applicable input exposes the correct programmatically determinable purpose.
1.3.5.failed: An applicable input lacks correct programmatic purpose metadata.
1.3.5.inapplicable: No inputs match the normative purposes, or the technology cannot support purpose identification.
limitations: Retain programmatic input-purpose metadata; spoken labels alone cannot establish the purpose declaration.

1.4.1.applicability: Color conveying information, action, response, or a distinction.
actions: Compare normal, selected, invalid, disabled, chart, and link states for color-dependent meaning.
Remove or neutralize color and inspect whether text, shape, pattern, or another visual cue preserves the meaning.
1.4.1.passed: Every meaningful color distinction has another visual means of conveying the same information.
1.4.1.failed: Meaning or operation depends on color alone.
1.4.1.inapplicable: Color conveys no information or distinction in the observed states.

1.4.2.applicability: Audio playing automatically for more than three seconds.
actions: Load initial and dynamic states without requesting playback and observe automatic audio duration.
Locate and operate pause/stop or independent audio volume controls using the keyboard and reader.
1.4.2.passed: Applicable audio can be paused or stopped, or its volume controlled independently of system volume.
1.4.2.failed: Automatic audio exceeds three seconds without an accepted control.
1.4.2.inapplicable: No audio plays automatically for more than three seconds.

1.4.3.applicability: Text and images of text, except logos, incidental content, and inactive controls.
actions: Measure text/background contrast across states, images, gradients, and overlays; record size and weight.
Apply 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for qualifying large text; document each normative exception.
1.4.3.passed: Every applicable text sample meets its required contrast ratio.
1.4.3.failed: An applicable text sample falls below its required ratio.
1.4.3.inapplicable: All scoped text falls within documented normative exceptions.

1.4.4.applicability: Text, excluding captions and images of text.
actions: Increase text to 200 percent without assistive technology and capture before/after states.
Operate the interface and inspect clipping, overlap, missing content, and loss of controls at that size.
1.4.4.passed: All applicable text resizes to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
1.4.4.failed: Applicable text cannot resize or the resized state loses content or functionality.
1.4.4.inapplicable: The scope contains only excluded captions or images of text.

1.4.5.applicability: Images of text where the technology can provide the intended presentation using text.
actions: Inventory text rendered as images and compare available text presentation.
Test customization and document whether a particular presentation is essential, including logotype exceptions.
1.4.5.passed: Text is used, or every image of text is customizable or essential under the normative exception.
1.4.5.failed: A nonessential, noncustomizable image replaces text the technology could render.
1.4.5.inapplicable: There are no applicable images of text.

1.4.10.applicability: Content except parts requiring two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.
actions: Render vertical content at 320 CSS pixels wide, or horizontal content at 256 CSS pixels high.
Operate controls and inspect lost content and two-direction scrolling; assess exempt parts separately from surrounding content.
1.4.10.passed: Applicable content reflows without loss or scrolling in two dimensions.
1.4.10.failed: Nonexempt content loses information/functionality or requires two-direction scrolling.
1.4.10.inapplicable: All scoped content requires two-dimensional layout; document the usage or meaning that requires it.

1.4.11.applicability: Visual information needed to identify active controls, states, or meaningful graphical objects.
actions: Inventory required control boundaries, state indicators, icons, charts, and focus indicators.
Measure contrast against adjacent colors for each state and document unmodified user-agent and essential-presentation exceptions.
1.4.11.passed: Required visual information has at least 3:1 contrast against adjacent colors, or meets a normative exception.
1.4.11.failed: Required nonexempt visual information has contrast below 3:1.
1.4.11.inapplicable: No active controls or meaningful graphics need author-defined visual information.

1.4.12.applicability: Markup-language content supporting text spacing properties.
actions: Apply all supported spacing overrides together: line height 1.5, paragraph spacing 2, letter spacing 0.12, and word spacing 0.16 times font size.
Inspect and operate all states for lost content or functionality; language/script exceptions exclude only properties not used by that language.
1.4.12.passed: The combined spacing overrides cause no loss of content or functionality.
1.4.12.failed: The required spacing overrides hide content or prevent operation.
1.4.12.inapplicable: Only when the technology supports none of the required spacing properties. Language exceptions do not exempt testing the remaining properties.

1.4.13.applicability: Additional content triggered and dismissed by pointer hover or keyboard focus.
actions: Trigger every tooltip, popup, and hover/focus disclosure using pointer and keyboard separately.
Test dismissal without moving focus/pointer, hover over the disclosure, and persistence until dismissed or invalid.
1.4.13.passed: Each applicable disclosure is dismissible, hoverable, and persistent, allowing the criterion's explicit exceptions.
1.4.13.failed: A nonexempt disclosure fails dismissal, hoverability, or persistence.
1.4.13.inapplicable: No author-controlled additional content appears on hover or focus.

2.1.1.applicability: All functionality except input whose underlying function requires a movement path.
actions: Inventory functions and complete each task using only the keyboard, including dialogs and custom widgets.
Test alternate keyboard operation and timing requirements; distinguish handwriting/drawing from dragging a control.
2.1.1.passed: Every nonexempt function operates through a keyboard interface without specific keystroke timing.
2.1.1.failed: A nonexempt function needs pointer input or specific keystroke timing.
2.1.1.inapplicable: No functionality exists, or all scoped functions have documented path-dependent exceptions.

actions: Enter each component with the keyboard, including embedded content and dialogs.
Leave using standard navigation; test any documented nonstandard exit instructions and focus return.
2.1.2.passed: Keyboard focus can leave every component, with instructions for any nonstandard exit method.
2.1.2.failed: Focus becomes trapped or a required nonstandard exit lacks instructions.
2.1.2.inapplicable: No component can receive keyboard focus.

2.1.4.applicability: Shortcuts using only letters, punctuation, numbers, or symbols.
actions: Inventory character-key shortcuts and test them while focus is inside and outside the associated control.
Test disabling or remapping to include nonprinting keys; verify focus-only activation alternatives.
2.1.4.passed: Every character shortcut can be disabled/remapped or is active only when its control has focus.
2.1.4.failed: A character shortcut remains active globally without an accepted disabling or remapping option.
2.1.4.inapplicable: The scope has no character-only shortcuts.

2.2.1.applicability: Time limits set by content, including session expiry and temporary responses.
actions: Inventory limits and observe warnings, expiry, and recovery using authorized test data.
Test turning off or adjusting limits, or extending with at least 20 seconds warning and ten extensions; document exceptions.
2.2.1.passed: Each time limit meets an accepted adjustment mechanism or a documented normative exception.
2.2.1.failed: A nonexempt limit expires without a qualifying adjustment or extension mechanism.
2.2.1.inapplicable: No content-imposed time limit exists; document any real-time, essential, or over-20-hour exception.

2.2.2.applicability: Automatic moving, blinking, scrolling, or updating information presented alongside other content.
actions: Observe motion duration and automatic updates in initial and dynamic states.
Operate pause/stop/hide controls for motion over five seconds and pause/stop/hide/frequency controls for updates.
2.2.2.passed: All applicable motion and updates have accepted controls or documented essential exceptions.
2.2.2.failed: Nonessential applicable motion or updates cannot be controlled as required.
2.2.2.inapplicable: No applicable automatic information is presented alongside other content.

2.3.1.applicability: Flashing content, including video, animation, and state transitions.
actions: Inventory flashing content without prolonged viewing; obtain recordings or source timing where safe.
Measure flashes per second or use validated general/red flash threshold analysis with area and luminance evidence.
2.3.1.passed: Content flashes no more than three times per second or stays below the general and red flash thresholds.
2.3.1.failed: Measured content exceeds three flashes per second and the applicable flash thresholds.
2.3.1.inapplicable: The inventory and observations show no flashing content.
limitations: Unaided visual judgment cannot establish flash thresholds; missing validated measurement remains uncertain.

2.4.1.applicability: Blocks repeated across a set of pages.
actions: Identify repeated blocks and navigate their bypass mechanisms with keyboard and real reader.
Verify that bypass reaches the intended content on every represented template and state.
2.4.1.passed: An operable mechanism bypasses each repeated block on the scoped page set.
2.4.1.failed: A repeated block has no operable bypass mechanism.
2.4.1.inapplicable: There are no blocks repeated across scoped pages.

2.4.2.applicability: Every scoped web page, including routes with changed purpose.
actions: Read the document title after loading each route and meaningful navigation state.
Compare the title with the page's topic or purpose and distinguish separate documents.
2.4.2.passed: Each document has a title describing its topic or purpose.
2.4.2.failed: A document's title is absent or fails to describe its topic or purpose.
2.4.2.inapplicable: Only for a non-web target where the web-page requirement cannot be applied; record the software guidance used.

2.4.3.applicability: Sequential focus navigation where order affects meaning or operation.
actions: Traverse focus in both directions through initial, dialog, error, and changed states.
Compare the sequence and focus restoration with the task's meaning and operation.
2.4.3.passed: Every sequential focus order preserves meaning and operability.
2.4.3.failed: A focus sequence loses meaning, skips required controls, or prevents operation.
2.4.3.inapplicable: No sequentially navigable components affect meaning or operation.

actions: Inventory links and determine each destination or action without submitting destructive operations.
Compare link names plus programmatically determined context with their purposes; examine ambiguity to users generally.
2.4.4.passed: Every link's purpose is determinable from its text/context, except purpose ambiguous to users generally.
2.4.4.failed: A nonexempt link purpose cannot be determined from link text and permitted programmatic context.
2.4.4.inapplicable: There are no links in the scoped states.

2.4.5.applicability: Pages within a set, except results of or steps in a process.
actions: Inventory non-process pages and locate them through navigation, search, sitemap, or other available methods.
Verify at least two distinct methods reach each applicable page, with process exceptions recorded.
2.4.5.passed: Every applicable page can be located in more than one way.
2.4.5.failed: An applicable page has fewer than two ways to locate it.
2.4.5.inapplicable: The scope is a single standalone page or consists entirely of process steps/results.

2.4.6.applicability: Headings and labels that are present.
actions: Collect headings and labels in all observed states and inspect the content or controls they identify.
Compare each heading/label with its topic or purpose, including repeated and icon-only controls.
2.4.6.passed: Each heading and label describes its topic or purpose.
2.4.6.failed: A present heading or label is misleading or does not describe its topic or purpose.
2.4.6.inapplicable: No headings or labels are present; assess required labels under other applicable criteria.

actions: Focus every keyboard-operable control, including nested widgets and changed states.
Capture its visible focus indicator and verify an available mode preserves it during keyboard operation.
2.4.7.passed: A visible keyboard focus indicator is available for every keyboard-operable interface.
2.4.7.failed: Keyboard focus cannot be visually located on an applicable interface.
2.4.7.inapplicable: The scope has no keyboard-operable interface.

2.4.11.applicability: Components receiving keyboard focus in author-created content.
actions: Move focus through every control with sticky layers, dialogs, cookie notices, and zoomed layouts present.
Capture each focused component and test scrolling/revealing without moving focus for user-opened content.
2.4.11.passed: Every focused component is at least partly visible, allowing the criterion's documented reveal exceptions.
2.4.11.failed: Author content entirely hides a focused component without an accepted reveal mechanism.
2.4.11.inapplicable: No user-interface component receives keyboard focus.

2.5.1.applicability: Multipoint or path-based gestures, excluding essential gestures and user-agent functionality.
actions: Inventory pinch, swipe-path, drawing, and multi-pointer functions.
Complete each nonessential function with a single pointer without a path-based gesture; keyboard alone is insufficient.
2.5.1.passed: Every nonessential gesture function has a single-pointer alternative requiring no path gesture.
2.5.1.failed: A nonessential multipoint/path gesture is the only pointer operation for a function.
2.5.1.inapplicable: No author-controlled multipoint or path-based gestures exist, or all are documented as essential.

2.5.2.applicability: Functions operated with a single pointer.
actions: Inspect and exercise pointer down/up behavior with authorized test data.
Test abort before release, undo after completion, up-event reversal, and any essential down-event exceptions.
2.5.2.passed: Each function avoids down-event completion or supplies a qualifying abort, undo, reversal, or essential exception.
2.5.2.failed: A nonessential down-event action completes without an accepted cancellation mechanism.
2.5.2.inapplicable: No functions use a single pointer.

2.5.3.applicability: Controls with visible text or images of text as labels.
actions: Inventory visible control labels and read their programmatic accessible names.
Compare the visible words with the name, including punctuation, symbol, and mathematical-expression treatment.
2.5.3.passed: Each applicable accessible name contains its visible label text.
2.5.3.failed: A control's accessible name omits or changes the visible label words.
2.5.3.inapplicable: There are no controls with visible text labels.

2.5.4.applicability: Functions activated by device or user motion.
actions: Inspect product controls and documentation for motion-operated functions and observe available hardware support.
Test interface alternatives and disabling motion response; document essential or accessibility-supported exceptions.
2.5.4.passed: Motion functions have interface alternatives and can be disabled, or meet a documented normative exception.
2.5.4.failed: A nonexempt motion function lacks an interface alternative or cannot be disabled.
2.5.4.inapplicable: No motion-operated functions exist; absent host sensors alone do not establish inapplicability.

2.5.7.applicability: Author-defined functions using dragging, excluding essential dragging.
actions: Inventory sortable lists, sliders, maps, uploads, and other dragging functions.
Complete each function using one pointer without dragging; test documented essential exceptions.
2.5.7.passed: Each nonessential dragging function has a single-pointer operation without dragging.
2.5.7.failed: A nonessential dragging function lacks a non-dragging pointer alternative.
2.5.7.inapplicable: No author-defined dragging functions exist, or all dragging is essential under the criterion.

actions: Measure each target's CSS-pixel dimensions and neighboring target geometry in every layout/state.
Test 24-by-24 sizing or the 24-pixel circle spacing rule; document equivalent, inline, user-agent, and essential exceptions.
2.5.8.passed: Every pointer target meets minimum size/spacing or an explicit normative exception.
2.5.8.failed: A nonexempt target is undersized and fails the required spacing.
2.5.8.inapplicable: There are no pointer targets in scope.

actions: Determine the page's primary language and inspect its programmatic declaration.
Read language-dependent content with a configured real reader and compare declarations with the content.
3.1.1.passed: The page's default human language is programmatically determinable and correctly identified.
3.1.1.failed: The page's language declaration is missing or incorrect.
3.1.1.inapplicable: A page normally requires a default language; unresolved language knowledge is uncertain, not inapplicable.

3.1.2.applicability: Passages or phrases in a language different from the page's default.
actions: Find language changes and inspect programmatic language metadata for each passage.
Read representative changes with the real reader; distinguish names, technical terms, indeterminate words, and vernacular.
3.1.2.passed: All nonexempt language changes are correctly programmatically identified.
3.1.2.failed: A nonexempt language change lacks correct programmatic identification.
3.1.2.inapplicable: There are no nonexempt passages in another language, with documented exceptions.

actions: Focus each control without activating it and capture any state, document, or window change.
Distinguish changes of context from content updates and compare the before/after focus location.
3.2.1.passed: Receiving focus never initiates a change of context.
3.2.1.failed: Focus alone initiates a change of context.

3.2.2.applicability: Changes to the setting of a user-interface component.
actions: Inspect instructions, then change each setting using authorized test data without explicit submission.
Capture context changes and determine whether the user was advised before operating the component.
3.2.2.passed: Setting changes avoid context changes or the user receives advance advice.
3.2.2.failed: A setting change initiates an unannounced change of context.
3.2.2.inapplicable: No component setting can be changed.

3.2.3.applicability: Navigation mechanisms repeated within a set of pages.
actions: Compare repeated navigation across scoped templates and authenticated states.
Record each mechanism's relative order and distinguish changes initiated by the user.
3.2.3.passed: Repeated navigation occurs in the same relative order except for user-initiated changes.
3.2.3.failed: Repeated navigation changes relative order without user initiation.
3.2.3.inapplicable: There are no repeated navigation mechanisms across the page set.

3.2.4.applicability: Components with the same functionality within a set of pages.
actions: Group controls by actual function across scoped pages, including icon and text variants.
Compare identification of equivalent functions and distinguish intentional differences in function.
3.2.4.passed: Components with the same functionality are identified consistently.
3.2.4.failed: Components with the same functionality are identified inconsistently.
3.2.4.inapplicable: No components share functionality across scoped pages.

3.2.6.applicability: Repeated human contact, contact details, self-help, or automated contact mechanisms.
actions: Inventory qualifying help mechanisms across the page set and inspect their relative content order.
Compare repeated mechanisms, accounting for user-initiated changes and viewport variations under the criterion.
3.2.6.passed: Repeated qualifying help occurs in the same relative order unless the user initiates a change.
3.2.6.failed: Repeated help changes relative order without an accepted exception.
3.2.6.inapplicable: No qualifying help mechanism is repeated across the set of pages.

3.3.1.applicability: Input errors automatically detected by the content.
actions: Trigger required-field, format, range, and server validation errors with authorized test data.
Compare each detected error's text with the field in error and read it with the real reader.
3.3.1.passed: Each automatically detected error identifies the item and describes the error in text.
3.3.1.failed: A detected error lacks textual identification or description.
3.3.1.inapplicable: The scoped content detects no input errors; lack of access to validation remains uncertain.

actions: Inventory input requests and inspect labels, format guidance, required indicators, and grouped instructions.
Operate each field with the keyboard and reader and determine whether its requested input is understandable.
3.3.2.passed: Labels or instructions are provided when the content requires input.
3.3.2.failed: An input request lacks necessary labels or instructions.
3.3.2.inapplicable: The scope requires no user input.

3.3.3.applicability: Automatically detected input errors with known correction suggestions.
actions: Trigger errors and inspect available correction suggestions using authorized test data.
Compare suggestions with known correction paths; obtain context for security or purpose exceptions.
3.3.3.passed: Known correction suggestions are provided unless doing so jeopardizes security or content purpose.
3.3.3.failed: A known correction suggestion is withheld without an accepted exception.
3.3.3.inapplicable: There are no applicable detected errors or known suggestions; document security/purpose exceptions.

3.3.4.applicability: Legal/financial commitments, changes/deletions to user-controlled stored data, or submission of test responses.
actions: Identify qualifying submissions and inspect reversibility, validation, and review/correction mechanisms.
Exercise authorized staging/test transactions through confirmation; stop before irreversible production actions.
3.3.4.passed: Each qualifying submission is reversible, checked with correction opportunities, or confirmed after review/correction.
3.3.4.failed: A qualifying submission has none of the accepted error-prevention mechanisms.
3.3.4.inapplicable: There are no qualifying submissions; lack of submission authorization alone is insufficient.

3.3.7.applicability: Information entered by or provided to the user that is requested again within the same process.
actions: Complete ordered process steps and record every repeated request using authorized test data.
Test automatic population or user selection; document essential, security, and obsolete-information exceptions.
3.3.7.passed: Repeated information is populated/selectable or meets a documented exception.
3.3.7.failed: A nonexempt process requires the user to enter the same information again.
3.3.7.inapplicable: The process never requests previously supplied information again.

3.3.8.applicability: Every authentication step, including recovery and multifactor branches.
actions: Walk all authentication branches with test accounts; identify memorization, transcription, and puzzle requirements.
Test password-manager/autofill/paste support and noncognitive alternatives; document object-recognition/personal-content exceptions.
3.3.8.passed: Every cognitive function test has an accepted alternative, assistance mechanism, or normative exception.
3.3.8.failed: An authentication step requires a nonexempt cognitive function test without accepted assistance or alternatives.
3.3.8.inapplicable: The scoped product has no authentication process.

4.1.1.applicability: Markup-language content under WCAG 2.1; this criterion is removed from WCAG 2.2.
actions: Validate markup for complete tags, proper nesting, duplicate attributes, and unique IDs.
Compare each error with the markup specification's permitted syntax and retain the validation output.
4.1.1.passed: Markup meets the criterion's parsing conditions or the specification explicitly permits the syntax.
4.1.1.failed: Markup violates a required parsing condition without a specification allowance.
4.1.1.inapplicable: The target is not implemented using a markup language.
limitations: Retain markup-validator output covering every parsing condition; reader announcements alone cannot prove parsing.

4.1.2.applicability: All user-interface components, including custom and dynamically changed controls.
actions: Inventory controls and inspect programmatic names, roles, states, properties, and values with a real reader.
Operate each control and change user-settable values; compare announced updates and programmatic semantics with behavior.
4.1.2.passed: Names/roles are determinable, user-settable states/values are programmatic, and changes notify user agents and AT.
4.1.2.failed: A control lacks required semantics, user-settable properties, or notification of changes.

4.1.3.applicability: Status messages that do not constitute a change of context.
actions: Trigger success, result-count, waiting, progress, and error status messages while preserving focus.
Record real-reader announcements and inspect roles/properties without moving focus to the message.
4.1.3.passed: Each applicable status message is programmatically determinable and presented by AT without receiving focus.
4.1.3.failed: An applicable status message cannot be presented by AT without focus.
4.1.3.inapplicable: No status messages occur in the exercised functionality.
